description: The Blackrock Loop in the Ballyhoura Mountains is a rewarding circular trail that climbs through forest tracks and open hillside to reach the summit of Seefin Mountain. The walk begins from the Ballyhoura car park and follows well-marked paths that wind gradually uphill through dense conifer woodland. As the route gains height, occasional clearings reveal expansive views across the Ballyhoura range and the surrounding valleys. Leaving the shelter of the trees, the trail emerges onto open moorland where heather and coarse grasses dominate. From here, the final ascent to Seefin Mountain offers a broad panorama of the Galtee Mountains to the east and the plains of Limerick stretching away to the west. On clear days, the view from the summit is one of the highlights of the Ballyhoura region, with wind turbines on nearby ridges and rolling farmland below. After reaching Seefin, the route descends gently along a different path, looping back through forest tracks lined with pine, spruce, and occasional birch. The mixture of wooded trails, upland heath, and open ridge walking makes this route particularly varied. Wildlife is common in the quieter sections, with chances to spot sika deer and a range of upland bird species. The trail is well maintained and clearly signposted, though the higher ground can be exposed in poor weather. Good footwear is essential, especially after rain when some sections can become soft underfoot. The Blackrock Loop provides an excellent introduction to the Ballyhoura Mountains, combining woodland walking with a scenic mountain summit and far-reaching views across the Munster landscape.
